not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is roxithromycin, a 14-membered macrolide with desosamine and cladinose sugars and a 9-oxime ether side chain; it shares its core scaffold with erythromycin (M04) and clarithromycin (M01), for which the supplied records show substantial oral exposure and intestinal absorption.

L3 human oral-exposure records for erythromycin, clarithromycin, and azithromycin show substantial plasma AUC/Cmax after oral dosing, e.g., erythromycin Cmax 2.7 mg/L at steady state after 250 mg oral (C133), clarithromycin AUCτ 18,222 ng·h/mL and Cmax 2458 ng/mL after 500 mg BID (C148/C108), and azithromycin AUC0-inf about 4,300–5,900 ng·h/mL after 500 mg oral (C101/C117/C129).

L4 permeability records show erythromycin has high apical-to-basolateral permeability in MDCKII-MDR1 (Papp A-B 1.56 ×10^-3 cm/s, C167) with P-gp-mediated efflux (B-A 6.93 ×10^-3, C189); P-gp inhibition increases A-B to 5.14 ×10^-3 (C163). Clarithromycin Caco-2 a→b transport is increased by P-gp/MRP inhibitors (C155, C178), indicating efflux but not absence of absorption.

L4 solubility/dissolution records for the same macrolide class are consistent with adequate intestinal dissolution: clarithromycin dissolution >94% at pH 4.5 (C150) and ~95% at pH 5 (C164), with saturation solubility ~14–18 mg/mL at pH 5 (C169/C173/C174) and ~2–3 mg/mL at pH 6.8 (C154/C184/C193); azithromycin aqueous solubility is ~4.5–5 mg/mL at pH 6.5 (C153/C165).

The L1/L2 low-F gold records are for structurally unrelated classes (corticosteroids, aminoglycosides, pseudo-tetrasaccharide, saponin, glycopeptide, tetracycline, nucleoside, flavonoid glycoside) and have low transferability to the query macrolide; they do not provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20% in roxithromycin.
The physicochemical prior (high MW, TPSA, HBD/HBA, ionization) is an uncertain prior and is outweighed by empirical oral exposure and absorption/permeability evidence for close macrolide analogs.

evidence_gaps: No direct roxithromycin-specific absolute oral bioavailability measurement or matched oral-versus-IV AUC is present in the supplied records.
L4 records are for close macrolide analogs (erythromycin, clarithromycin, azithromycin) and some formulation-specific solubility/dissolution studies, not roxithromycin itself.
No query-specific gut-wall metabolism or first-pass data are available at this level.
The low-F L1/L2 contexts are structurally unrelated and have low transferability to the query macrolide.

The low-F L1/L2 contexts are structurally unrelated and do not transfer. Prediction remains high, with high confidence.
